question: A 28-year-old man from Assam presents with fever for 5 days, impaired consciousness (GCS 11), and a peripheral blood smear showing P. falciparum with >5% parasitaemia. What is the FIRST-LINE treatment for his condition?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oral ACT is first-line for uncomplicated falciparum malaria. This patient has severe malaria (altered consciousness, high parasitaemia), which requires parenteral artesunate — oral treatment is inadequate.

answers.text: Intravenous artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, 24 hours, then once daily until oral therapy is tolerated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO and NVBDCP guidelines recommend IV artesunate as first-line for severe falciparum malaria. It is superior to IV quinine in efficacy and safety and should be started immediately.

IV quinine was the previous standard but is now second-line. IV artesunate is preferred due to superior efficacy in reducing mortality and fewer adverse effects (notably, less hypoglycaemia and cardiac toxicity).

answers.text: Chloroquine 600 mg base stat followed by 300 mg at 6, 24, 48 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chloroquine is ineffective against P. falciparum in India due to widespread resistance. It must never be used for falciparum malaria.

overallFeedback.feedback: Severe malaria criteria: altered sensorium, respiratory distress, >5% parasitaemia, haemoglobinuria, acute renal/hepatic failure, hypoglycaemia. Any one → IV artesunate immediately.
Well done. IV artesunate is the single most important treatment decision in severe falciparum malaria and must be initiated without delay.
